assumptions: USD million except per-episode rates. Fictional bundled payment is earned per completed eligible episode; transfers outside bundle are not eligible. Confirmed outlier reimbursement separately earned.

evidence.text: [Episode registry] 2,400 admissions: 2,100 completed eligible episodes, 200 transfers to another hospital before completion, 100 still open at year end. Base payment $9,000 per eligible episode.
[Payer notice] Among the 2,100 completed episodes, 120 qualify for additional outlier payment $5,000 each; 30 applications remain unapproved and are not in the 120.
[Cost ledger] Completed episode treatment cost $14.4m, transfer cost $1.1m, open episode expense $0.8m. All costs expensed in this toy. Central expense $2.2m.
[Settlement] Payer cash receipts $17.5m, opening receivable $1.4m, no other billing or collections.
[Performance memo] Administrator quotes 2,400 admissions as completed episodes and claims all outlier applications will be accepted.

qas.question: Determine base bundled consideration for the verified completed episodes.
What additional consideration is earned from approved outlier cases?
Reconcile closing payer receivable under the bundle contract.
Calculate hospital operating result after costs of all three patient groups.
By how much would using all admissions overstate base bundle revenue?
What is the completed eligible episode share of admissions?
Why are transfer and open-episode costs not removed when excluding their revenue?
qas.answer: Treatment resources were consumed and the toy expenses those costs, independently of payer eligibility.

qas.question: Can the payer's final settlement of 30 pending outlier applications be estimated exactly?
qas.answer: No. The outcome of adjudication is not supplied.

assumptions: USD million; million tonnes. A fictional rail agreement collects deficiency charges for unused annual capacity. A portion creates a future makeup right, so only the nonrefundable portion without future service is recognized immediately.

evidence.text: [Contract] Annual reserved volume 5m tonnes at $12/t. Shipper actually transports 4m tonnes and pays all transported freight. Deficiency charge is $12 per unused tonne.
[Makeup clause] 70% of deficiency charge gives a right to future transport during next year. Remaining 30% has no future obligation and is earned when the year closes.
[Settlement] All charges billed and paid at year end. No opening makeup liability or prior rights exercised.
[Cost] Variable cost $7 per actual tonne, fixed cash expense 15m. No other charges or tax.
[Operations] Capacity report describes 5m reserved tonnes as transported volume; commercial deck shows all billed amounts as revenue.

qas.question: Find actual transported freight revenue.
Compute the cash deficiency payment for unused reserved tonnes.
Determine the earned portion of the deficiency charge.
What makeup liability remains for next year's freight service?
Calculate operating profit before depreciation, using earned consideration only.
Calculate cash surplus before capital expenditure.
Why is the full billed 60m not current revenue?
qas.answer: 8.4m relates to an outstanding makeup service right.

qas.question: Can next year's physical utilization be calculated from the makeup liability?
qas.answer: No. Exercise of the right and other bookings are unknown.

assumptions: USD million; million minutes. The fictional operator recognizes wholesale roaming income on inbound usage and expense on outbound usage. Bilateral cash netting does not change gross recognition.

evidence.text: [Roaming statement] Inbound visitors use 60m minutes at $.08/min; own subscribers abroad use 45m minutes at $.10/min. No data charges.
[Agreement] Partner applies 10% volume discount to inbound consideration if inbound minutes exceed 50m; applies to all inbound minutes once met. Outbound expense has no discount.
[Clearing house] Opening net payable .3m; settlement at year end is .5m cash paid by operator. All usage and adjustments billed, no other items.
[Retail] Own subscriber roaming fees earned 7m, direct support cost 1.2m; wholesale roaming costs excluded from support cost.
[Deck] Treasurer reports net clearing payment as wholesale expense; no partner-by-partner credit terms.

qas.question: Calculate gross inbound wholesale revenue before discount.
Determine inbound wholesale revenue net of earned volume discount.
Find recognized outbound wholesale roaming expense.
Reconcile the net clearing balance after the .5m payment, with payable positive.
What contribution results from inbound, outbound, retail roaming and support?
What inbound discount amount became effective?
Why is the .5m cash settlement not the wholesale expense?
qas.answer: It settles net current income/expense and opening payable; accrual outbound expense is 4.5m.

qas.question: Can the legal right to present gross receivables and payables net on the balance sheet be established?
qas.answer: No. Cash clearing alone does not establish all offset criteria; no detailed terms are given.

assumptions: USD million; thousand tickets. Toy operating carrier earns prorated flight consideration for segments it operates; selling another carrier's segment creates payable, not revenue. All flights completed in period.

evidence.text: [Ticket sales] Airline sells 100k itineraries at $600, each containing own segment allocated $350 and partner segment $250. All tickets flown, cash collected.
[Interline sales] Partner sells 40k itineraries containing this airline's segment allocated $300 each; airline has performed those flights and is owed the allocated amount.
[Clearing] Opening partner payable 4m, opening receivable 2m. Cash remitted 23m, cash collected from partner 11m. No netting of balance-sheet items in toy.
[Costs] Operating own flown segments costs 30m, selling expense 5m. No cost of providing partner segment beyond paying its share.
[Report] Sales deck counts all 60m ticket sales as own passenger revenue; excludes partner-sold flown segments.

qas.question: What consideration belongs to own segments on tickets sold directly?
Find current partner payable arising from the direct itinerary sales.
Determine revenue earned from partner-sold tickets on own aircraft.
What is the correct total passenger revenue from these interline arrangements?
Reconcile ending gross interline payable.
Reconcile ending gross interline receivable.
Explain why the sales deck's 60m misstates revenue in two directions.
qas.answer: It includes 25m earned by partner and omits 12m earned on partner-sold tickets; correct revenue is 47m.

qas.question: Could a route-specific profit margin be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Own flight costs are aggregated without route attribution.

assumptions: USD million; thousand kg. Toy seed grower receives price by certified grade; failed seed is sold as grain separately. Production cost incurred on all seed; price bonus applies accepted premium grade only.

evidence.text: [Harvest] 900k kg of seed harvested. Lab certifies 600k premium grade, 200k standard, 100k rejected. No quantity loss.
[Purchase agreement] Premium $4/kg plus $.50 quality bonus; standard $3/kg; rejected seed not purchased by seed buyer, sold separately as grain at $.40/kg.
[Cost] Field cost $1.8m; testing and sorting $.25m; packaging $.30/kg on accepted seed only; grain sale has $.05/kg handling cost.
[Payment] All accepted seed billed; cash from seed buyer 2.9m; grain cash received immediately. No opening receivable.
[Agronomy] No farm area, rainfall, germination distribution or seed variety detail.

qas.question: Find gross premium-grade sales including quality bonus.
What revenue comes from rejected seed sold as ordinary grain?
Calculate seed-buyer receivable after cash collections.
Determine total packaging and grain handling expense.
Find crop contribution after all disclosed costs.
What percentage of the harvest meets either certified seed grade?
Should rejected seed be valued at the standard seed contract price?
qas.answer: No. The buyer rejects it; the separate grain sale establishes its earned consideration.

qas.question: Can germination failure be attributed to drought?
qas.answer: No. The agronomy records contain neither weather nor causal evidence.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional donor-restricted endowment invests principal perpetually; spending policy releases a stipulated amount for eligible educational costs only. Investment returns belong to restricted fund until released.

evidence.text: [Endowment balances] Opening restricted investments 200m; new restricted gifts 20m. Investment return 18m, of which 8m cash and 10m unrealized. No investment sales.
[Spending rule] Board-approved spending appropriation is 4% of opening balance. Only eligible scholarship payments release donor restrictions; appropriation itself is not unrestricted cash.
[Scholarships] Eligible cash awards 6m this year; another 2m planned but not awarded. Cash awards funded by investment cash income.
[Operations] Unrestricted opening funds 12m, unrelated tuition surplus 3m, general capital purchases 4m. No other movements.
[Fundraising] Brochure calls the entire 20m gift unrestricted budget revenue; donor deeds explicitly require preservation of principal.

qas.question: Calculate the approved endowment appropriation limit.
Determine actual donor restriction release for awarded scholarships.
qas.answer: 6 million USD, not the full 8m appropriation.

qas.question: Find ending restricted endowment balance after investment return, gift and scholarships.
Calculate the appropriation still available for eligible awards within the stated policy.
qas.answer: Approved appropriation = 200×4% = 8m. Eligible awards already paid6; 8−6 = 2 million USD remains available under the policy, not automatically unrestricted cash.

qas.question: Determine unrestricted ending funds from unrelated operations and capital purchases.
qas.answer: 12+3−4=11 million USD; scholarship release funds equal awards.

qas.question: How much investment return is noncash in this endowment?
Why cannot the 20m restricted gift fund general capital purchases?
qas.answer: Donor deeds preserve principal and the gift is not unrestricted.

qas.question: Can long-run sustainable spending be established from one year's 18m return?
qas.answer: No. Future return, inflation and policy history are missing.

assumptions: USD million; thousand tonnes. Toy processor never owns customer's ore or recovered metal; earns toll on input tonnes and bonus on recovered metal above target. No commodity revenue belongs to processor.

evidence.text: [Toll agreement] Customer delivers 500k tonnes ore. Grade 2%; target recovery 85%, actual 90%. Base processing fee $45 per input tonne; performance bonus $500 per recovered metal tonne above target.
[Assay] All ore processed, recovered metal returned to customer. Customer's metal spot price $9,000/t, not processor consideration.
[Expense] Processing variable cost $30 per input tonne, fixed plant expense 4m. No inventory ownership or tax.
[Cash] Buyer pays base toll 20m and no bonus yet; all earned amounts billed; opening AR zero.
[Presentation] Plant management labels recovered metal value as plant turnover.

qas.question: Find contained metal in the ore feed.
Determine recovered metal above target, in tonnes.
Find earned performance bonus.
Calculate toll processor revenue excluding metal owned by customer.
Find processor operating result after variable and fixed costs.
Reconcile the outstanding processing invoice balance.
Why is recovered metal spot value excluded from processor sales?
qas.answer: Customer retains title to ore and metal; processor only earns toll and bonus.

qas.question: Can profitability of the ore owner's mine be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Extraction costs, taxes and sales terms are absent.

assumptions: USD million; million cubic meters; tonnes. Fictional wastewater tariff contains flow charge plus excess pollution load charge. Calculate excess per customer class, not across classes.

evidence.text: [Meter ledger] Domestic flow 12m m³ at $.60/m³; Industrial A flow 5m and Industrial B flow 3m, both $.80/m³.
[Pollution certificate] A pollution load 1,800 tonnes vs free allowance 1,200. B load 300 vs free allowance 500. Excess charged $1,000/t, no transfer of unused allowance.
[Operations] Treatment variable cost $.35/m³ on all flow; extra industrial pollution treatment expense .4m. Fixed costs 4m.
[Collection] All charges invoiced, cash receipts 12m; opening AR 1m. No bad debt or other flows.
[Slide] Commercial team nets B's unused allowance against A's excess.

qas.question: Find domestic wastewater flow-charge revenue.
Find industrial flow-charge revenue for both customers.
Calculate pollution surcharge on A under its separate allowance.
Determine total wastewater revenue including valid surcharge.
Calculate the operating result after treatment and fixed costs.
Find closing customer receivables on confirmed charges.
Why is a 400-tonne net excess inconsistent with the tariff?
qas.answer: B's unused 200 tonnes cannot offset A's excess 600; allowances are separate.

qas.question: Can water-quality improvement downstream be quantified?
qas.answer: No. No effluent monitoring or environmental baseline is given.
